relevance_note: The paper describes individual SSADH-deficient patients and carriers, e.g. 'A pathogenic homozygous mutation of Aldh5A1 (p.Gly409Asp) was detected in the living sister'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. The paper is a review: cohort tables 1-4 are group counts only (n=68, 43, 34, 40) and give no rows. In-scope individuals: the Patient Vignette boy (no label; rule 6, 'unnamed person 1'); the SUDEP decedent of ref [15], her living sister and their two parents (heterozygote carriers); the parent and sibling with heterozygosity in one family of ref [7]; the two adolescent brothers of ref [27]; the 2 1/2-year-old boy of ref [33]; and three figure-legend patients (Figure 2 and Figure 5 reprinted from Pearl et al. Neurology 2009, Figure 3 from Acosta et al. 2010), labelled by rule 4 with the reference as printed; these may overlap with each other or with the vignette patient, but the paper does not say so, so they are not merged. Not given rows: the 'heterozygote control' in Figure 5 (no individual-level fact), the eight TMS patient/parent sets, the ten sleep-study patients and the 33-patient cohort (group-level only), and the implied affected proband of the ref [7] family (not described). The parents of the ref [15] sisters are recorded as carrying p.Gly409Asp because they are called heterozygote carriers right after that mutation is named; the sentence itself does not repeat the variant. Inheritance for the homozygous sisters is 'not reported': both parents are carriers, but the enum has no biparental value; the statement is in parental_testing_statement. Ref [7] parent and sibling: the sentence gives the four features to 'a parent and sibling' jointly, recorded for each; heterozygosity is stated for the family and read as applying to them; no variant or gene symbol is printed. Ref [27] diagnosis comes from the reference-list title. Ref [33] boy's age (2 1/2 years) is the age at taurine treatment/report of the case and fits no age field, so is left not reported; his improved gait, coordination, energy and behaviour imply earlier problems but are not stated as features. Vignette: 'severe hyperactivity' was not mapped to the checklist item 'attention problems or ADHD' (no inattention or ADHD stated). Drug-associated lethargy (valproate) and insomnia (higher taurine doses) are recorded as observed with the drug in severity_or_detail. No contradictions found. No stacked cells.
